title: unified-rollouts-canary-shadow-ab-autorollback-enhancements
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: rolling updates for model variants increasingly rely on combined canary / A-B / shadow traffic flows with automated rollback decisions. This PR adds telemetry hooks, improved metric matching, and safety guards to the autorollback engine so rollback decisions are both explainable and observable. Motivation: operators need clear signals (latency, error rate, quality regressions) plus quarantine paths when metrics are noisy. Summary of changes: 1) telemetry: emit per-route, per-variant composite metrics and sample-level traces used by the autorollback engine; 2) autorollback: extended composite-metric matcher to allow threshold windows and quorum-based quarantine; 3) safety guards: add manual quarantine + cooldown windows to avoid flip-flop across noisy metrics; 4) e2e: new integration tests that simulate canary and shadow traffic with injected regressions; 5) console: dashboard + incident view for autorollback triggers and recent quarantine events. Testing & validation: unit tests + integration e2e harness (simulated traffic) added, perf benchmarks run against a small model set to validate no observable latency regressions within SLO; staged rollout carried out on internal staging for 48h before merge. Rollout plan: feature gated, roll out to 10% of traffic on dedicated canary pools for 24h, monitor composite metric and alerts, then 50% followed by full roll when stable. Checklist: - [x] design review (ENG-1245) - [x] telemetry schema defined and backwards compatible - [x] e2e tests added - [x] perf benchmark within acceptable bounds - [x] docs + console dashboard updated - [x] migration-free (no DB schema change) Known limitations: composite matching currently supports up to 3 metrics per composite; follow-up work (ENG-1302) will generalize this to N metrics and add configurable weights. Related work: builds on prior autorollback refactor (pr-816544) and observability improvements (pr-82901).
